7.2    Sequence and Staging
7.2.1 Traffic Guidance Schemes Installation General
TTM measures must be installed, maintained, and removed in a planned and safe manner. Prior to
commencing, the Traffic Management Implementers must check and review the approved Traffic
Management Plan / Traffic Guidance Schemes, the worksite, and the proposed activity to ensure they are
complementary and are appropriate. This section provides best principles and practices guidance.
The Traffic Management Implementers must check the road environment, especially the “on the day”
traffic flows, to ensure that it is at an appropriate level for the Temporary Traffic Management intended. A
5-minute count of traffic should provide an appropriate estimate of volumes to reference against values
recorded in the Traffic Management Plan or the Traffic Guidance Schemes.
If the worksite and the approved Traffic Management Plan and Traffic Guidance Schemes are not
complementary, before occupying the worksite the Traffic Management Implementer must determine
whether they can:
     • make compliant adjustments (e.g. lengthen taper within tolerances) to the Traffic Guidance
         Schemes
     • contact the Delivery Supervisor, Roadworks Traffic Manager or Traffic Management Designer to
         approve relevant modifications (e.g. additional signs or distances outside of tolerances) to the
         Traffic Guidance Schemes.
     • contact the relevant Road Infrastructure Manager traffic control facility to initiate actions identified
         on the Traffic Guidance Schemes to be taken (e.g. change in the VMS, Variable Speed Limit Signs or
         Lane Usage Signage).

Where the Traffic Management Plan and Traffic Guidance Schemes cannot be suitably adjusted or
modified, the Traffic Management Implementer should advise the Delivery Supervisor that they are not
appropriate, and the works should be postponed.
All adjustments and authorised modifications are to be recorded on the Traffic Management Plan and
Traffic Guidance Schemes or on-site record.

7.2.2 Typical Installation Principles
Installation is typically carried out applying one of the processes in accordance with AGTTM Part 5 as
“short term – low impact works” to protect the Temporary Traffic Management staff. The examples in this
section are based on limiting high risk manoeuvrers during installation including U-Turns and loops
exposing workers to live traffic without protection.
Fundamental principles that should be complied with to ensure safety during this work activity are that:
    • travel should only be in a forward direction on any road
    • the Temporary Traffic Management vehicle may be used as added protection considering the:
            o availability of safe park up area(s) near the signage placement location
            o line of sight to approaching vehicles
            o visibility of the worker and Temporary Traffic Management vehicle to approaching vehicles
            o location of signage/devices on vehicle which need to be accessed
            o worker access to vehicle (e.g. not through crush zones)
            o available space on road shoulder or median
            o geometry/terrain of shoulder or median
            o distance between vehicle and travel path / shoulder drop off
            o Traffic Management Implementer proximity to ‘expected travel path while traversing
                 between vehicle and signage location
            o likely area in which the vehicle may move if impacted
            o availability of ‘gaps in traffic’ or lookout


 Traffic Management Plan 0922-01531 Rev. 6               OFFICIAL                                98 | P a g e
   •      turn around procedures must be conducted in a safe and legal manner
   •      Traffic Management Implementer must face the traffic when placing devices
   •      all workers must know their escape route at all times
   •      the vehicle mounted warning device must be operating and the hazard/arrow board used as
          required
      • all workers must wear correct PPE
      • a look out person/spotter must be used for all activities where required in accordance with AGTTM
          Part 5
      • full co-ordination of any ITS infrastructure which may assist the Traffic Guidance Schemes
          installation
      • the locations and types of devices are recorded in the diary
      • the Traffic Guidance Schemes is implemented as approved and a copy is available on site.
If it is considered too dangerous due to speed or volume to install the Traffic Guidance Schemes using the
protections defined in AGTTM Part 5, then consideration needs to be given to adopting a mobile convoy
(refer AGTTM Part 4) or other controls e.g. manual traffic control to hold traffic during installation under its
own Traffic Guidance Schemes (refer AGTTM Part 3). A different installation sequence may need to be
adopted to address any site-specific circumstances and can be approved by Traffic Management Designer
or other authorised person.

7.2.3 Installation Process
The general procedure for setting up a site is to:
   1. locate the work area using GPS, landmarks, side streets, chainage
   2. install devices as outlined in the Traffic Guidance Schemes for side streets first
   3. install devices as outlined in the Traffic Guidance Schemes for the non-working lane (un-affected
       direction)
   4. install devices as outlined in the Traffic Guidance Schemes for the working lane (affected direction)
       to complete installation.
   5. conduct a drive through inspection after all devices are in place and before work commences

All sign spacings and taper lengths will be noted on the Traffic Guidance Schemes and should be in
accordance with AGTTM Part 3.
7.2.4 Placement of Signs and Devices (AGTTM Part 6 Field Staff – Implementation and
      Operation)
The scenarios in AGTTM Part 6 Field Staff – Implementation and Operation Section 6.4 are designed to
encourage workers to review the safest installation process. Many factors can influence the appropriate
sequence for installation including but not limited to road geometry, hills, crests, curves, surface condition,
lane widths, shoulder width, traffic volumes, peak traffic flows, road user travel speed, road user make up
(e.g. % of heavy vehicles or cyclists), lighting and time of day, and weather.
If the Traffic Management Plan does not contain specific advice on the installation order for Traffic
Guidance Schemes, AGTTM Part 6, Section 6.4 gives several scenarios for the typical installation with
diagrams and steps to facilitate safe installation. These diagrams can be referred to when Traffic
Management Implementer’s are preparing for installation. The scenarios include:
     • Two-way road - lane closure
     • Two-way road (lateral shift)
     • Two-way road - lane closure with side roads
     • Multi-lane un-divided road - lane closure
     • Multi-lane divided road - left or right lane closure


 Traffic Management Plan 0922-01531 Rev. 6               OFFICIAL                                 99 | P a g e
 Always remember: A shadow vehicle displaying a vehicle mounted warning device (or TMA if applicable)
  must be used in advance of the Traffic Management Implementer’s installing signs and traffic control
                                       devices to protect workers.

Note: - Under the Vehicle Standards Regulations, vehicle mounted warning devices are approved and shall
not be used outside the limits of the road works.

7.2.5 Traffic Guidance Schemes Removal General (AGTTM Part 6 Field Staff –
      Implementation and Operation)
Removal of the TTM is usually considered more dangerous as crews may be fatigued, may be in a rush to
get home, and often as traffic management is removed there may be no advanced warning to alert drivers
to the presence of the workers. A risk assessment on each site should be taken into consideration prior to
the removal process. As part of this assessment, what has been happening on site (during that road work
period) should be also considered as it will represent the type of road user behaviours that have been
observed in that location.
Considerations should include the:
                a) duration of the roadwork                  e) speeds observed during road
                                                                work
                b) length of the site                        f) time of day
                c) complexity of the site                    g) type of conditions (haze / sun
                                                                glare etc.).
                d) original speed of the road

7.2.6 Typical Removal Principles
Removal is carried out applying one of the short-term low impact provisions in accordance with AGTTM
Part 5. The processes described in this section are based on limiting high risk manoeuvrers during removal
of the Traffic Guidance Schemes including U-Turns and loops exposing workers to live traffic without
protection.
Fundamental principles that should be complied with to ensure safety during this work activity are that:
    • travel should only be in a forward direction on any road
    • recovery of devices must be done in the reverse order using the same work method as for setting
        out
    • the TTM vehicle may be used as added protection considering the:
            o availability of safe park up areas near the signage placement location
            o line of sight to approaching vehicles
            o visibility of the worker and TTM vehicle to approaching vehicles
            o location of signage/devices on vehicle which need to be accessed
            o worker access to vehicle (e.g. not through crush zones)
            o available space on road shoulder or median
            o geometry/terrain of shoulder or median
            o distance between vehicle and travel path / shoulder drop off
            o Traffic Management Implementer proximity to expected travel path while traversing
                between vehicle and signage location
            o likely area in which the vehicle may move if impacted
            o availability of ‘gaps in traffic’ or lookout
    • turn around procedures must be conducted in a safe and legal manner.
    • Traffic Management Implementer must face the traffic when placing removing devices
    • all workers must know their escape route at all times


 Traffic Management Plan 0922-01531 Rev. 6             OFFICIAL                             100 | P a g e
   •      the vehicle mounted warning device must be operating and the hazard/arrow board used as
          required
      • all workers must wear correct PPE
      • a look out person/spotter must be used for all activities where required in accordance with AGTTM
          Part 5
      • full co-ordination of any ITS infrastructure which may assist the Traffic Guidance Schemes removal
      • the removal of the TTM signs and devices is recorded in the diary/sign register
      • conduct a final drive through of the site to ensure all devices are removed and all permanent signs
          are reinstated or uncovered.
If it is considered too dangerous due to speed or volume, then consideration needs to be given to adopting
a mobile convoy (refer to AGTTM Part 4) or other controls e.g. traffic control to hold traffic during removal
under its own Traffic Guidance Schemes. A different sequence may need to be adopted to address any site-
specific circumstances and can be approved by Traffic Management Designer.

7.2.7 Removal Process
The general procedure for removing a site is the:
       1. work area (devices in reverse order)
       2. affected side of roadway (signage in direction of travel)
       3. non-affected side of roadway (signage and devices in direction of travel)
       4. side roads (closure devices then signage in direction of travel)
       5. detours (in direction of travel).

7.2.8 Removal Order for Signs and Devices
The scenarios described in this Section are designed to encourage workers to review the safest process for
removal of a Traffic Guidance Schemes. Many factors can influence the sequence of removal including but
not limited to road geometry, hills, crests, curves, surface condition, lane widths, shoulder width, VPD,
peak traffic flows, road user travel speed, road user make up (e.g. % of heavy vehicles or cyclists), lighting
& time of day and weather.
AGTTM Part 6, Section 6.4 gives several scenarios for the typical removal with diagrams and steps to
facilitate safe removal. These diagrams can be referred to when Traffic Management Implementer’s are
preparing for removal. The scenarios include:
    • Two-way road - lane closure
    • Two-way road (lateral shift)
    • Two-way road - lane closure with side road intersections
    • Multi-lane un-divided road - lane closure
    • Multi-lane divided road - left or right lane closure

7.3      Traffic Control Devices
7.3.1    Requirements for Signs
All signs used shall conform to the designs and dimensions as shown in Australian Standard AS 1742.3,
AGTTM and the CoP.

Prior to installation, all signs and devices shall be checked by the Site Supervisor or a suitably qualified
person to ensure that they are in good condition and meet the following requirements:
    • Mechanical condition - It is required for items that are bent, broken or have surface damage not be
        of use.
    • Cleanliness - Items should be free from accumulated dirt, road grime or other contamination.


 Traffic Management Plan 0922-01531 Rev. 6              OFFICIAL                                101 | P a g e
    • Colour of fluorescent signs - fluorescent signs whose colour has faded to a point where they have
       lost their daylight impact shall be replaced.
    • Retro reflectivity. - Signs for night-time use whose retro reflectivity have degraded either from long
       use or from surface damage and does not meet the requirements of AS1906 need replacement.
    • Battery operated devices - shall be checked for lamp operation and battery condition.
Where signs either do not conform to the requirements of AS 1742.3, AGTTM or MRWA CoP or would fail
to pass any of the above checks, need replacement on notice.

Signs and devices shall be positioned and erected in accordance with the locations and spacing as shown
on the drawings. Erection and positioning of all signs are to be such that:
   • They are properly displayed and securely mounted;
   • They are within the driver’s line of sight;
   • They cannot be obscured from view;
   • They do not obscure other devices from the driver’s line of sight;
   • They do not become a possible hazard to workers or vehicles; and
   • They do not deflect traffic into an undesirable path.

A suitable opaque material shall cover signs and devices erected before they are required. Immediately
prior to the commencement of work, the cover may be detached. Where there is a potential for conflict of
information between existing signage and temporary signage erected for the purpose of traffic control, it is
required the existing signs be covered. It is required that the sign not be seen once the material covering is
placed on the sign, under all conditions i.e. day, night and wet weather. As to not cause damage, ensure
care to the existing signs when being covered by material or by adhesive tape.

7.3.1.1 Securing Signs and Devices
All signs and devices must be positioned and erected so that they are properly displayed and securely
mounted. The mountings should be stable in windy conditions and from the effects of high-speed moving
traffic. Signs must have additional support and be located with adequate lateral clearance from the
travelled way. The following scenarios are more likely to encounter fallen signs but are not limited to:
     • Where windy conditions are expected.
     • The road is used by road trains.
     • The permanent speed is 80km/h or greater.
The following options should be considered, using a risk management approach, to mitigate the risk of
signs falling over and/or not being properly displayed:
     • Sandbags (or similar) weighing 10-15kg on all legs.
     • Regular monitoring and maintenance in place to rectify fallen signs.
     • Use of Variable Message Signs in advance of the work site.
There may be a need to use a combination of the above methods on any particular site and some form of
monitoring the signs will always be required.

When using cones or bollards at high-risk locations and it is expected they will blow over due to windy
conditions, heavy vehicles or traffic speed the following must be considered to ensure additional stability:
   • Bollards to have a base of 12kg (or two 6kg bases can be used)
   • Cones to have a minimum of 6kg (or two 3kg cones stacked on top of each other.
Examples of high risk locations include but are not limited to lateral shifts on high speed roads, devices
separating the work area and devices delineation excavations.




 Traffic Management Plan 0922-01531 Rev. 6              OFFICIAL                               102 | P a g e
7.3.2    Tolerances on Positioning of Signs and Devices
Where a specific distance for the longitudinal positioning of signs or devices with respect to other items or
features is stated, for the spacing of delineating devices or for the length of tapers or markings, the
following tolerances may be applied: -
  1.   Positioning of signs, length of tapers or markings:
         (i).       Minimum, 10% less than the distances or lengths given.
        (ii).       Maximum, 25% more than the distances or lengths given.
  2.   Spacing of delineating devices:
         (i).       Maximum, 10% more than the spacing shown.
        (ii).       No minimum.
These tolerances shall not apply where a maximum, minimum or a range is already stated for a distance,
length or spacing.

7.3.3    Flashing Arrow Signs
Flashing arrow signs will comprise of a matrix of lamps in the form of an arrow that is flashed in a cyclic
manner to provide advance warning of a temporary diversion. It includes a backing board for the lamps
together with ancillary equipment necessary for mounting and operating the sign, and reducing its light
output (dimming) for night-time use. Flashing yellow signs shall be in accordance with AS/NZS 4192.
Illuminated flashing arrow signs may also be constructed of variable message LED type signs to provide the
same or a similar diversion arrow effect. The following three size designations must be used:
     Table 49: Illuminated Flashing Arrow Sign Size – Main Roads Code of Practice Section 6.10 Table 16
                                   Circumstance                                              Size
  Lane closures or mobile works on roads with a permanent speed of 60km/h or less.          Size A

                                                                                        1500 x 770 mm
                         Lane closures or mobile works on:
                                  • Any Freeway; or                                          Size C
     •   Multilane roads with a speed of 90km/h or more and 15,000vpd or more; or       2400 x 1200 mm
     •   Where a high level of long distance advance warning is desirable for safety.

High intensity flashing lamps may be used in conjunction with this sign provided that the lamps are either
appropriately shielded or laterally or vertically displaced from the edge of the sign to avoid visually
corrupting the arrow shape or its directional effect.

Requirements for the flashing of different patterns of the lights are as follows:
   • When traffic is expected to pass the sign on a particular side and can do so in safety, i.e. it is not
       required to seek a gap in oncoming traffic, the bar of the arrow and the barb directing traffic to that
       side shall be flashed.
   • When the sign is used to give a general warning of works activity ahead including mobile works, but
       either the sign is located clear of the traffic path or the display of an arrow would not be
       appropriate for some other reason, either the bar of the arrow only or the four corner lights at the
       extremities of the barbs shall be flashed. In the latter case diagonal pairs should be flashed
       alternately.

7.3.4    Delineation and Edge Clearance
Cones shall be used for delineation unless another treatment is specified in the Traffic Management Plan
or on the Traffic Guidance Schemes. All cones shall be at least 700 millimetres in height (and be fitted with
Class 1 reflective banner for night works) and constructed from fluorescent orange or red material that is
resilient to impact and will not damage vehicles when hit at low speed. Cones shall be designed to be
stable under reasonably expected wind conditions and air turbulence from passing traffic.

The base of the cones will be secured so that they are not dislodged by traffic. Cones will be inspected at
intervals necessary to ensure any misalignment or displacement is identified and corrected prior to this
causing disruption to traffic.

Where specified, temporary frangible or otherwise non-hazardous delineator posts or bollards may be
used for edge protection and taper delineation. Posts or bollards shall have a maximum dimension of 60
millimetres when measured along the longest side of a square or rectangular section or across the
diameter of a circular section. Base design shall permit easy fixing to either sealed or unsealed surfaces
and not intrude into traffic lanes greater than 50 millimetres from the face of the post or bollard.

All posts or bollards shall be erected in accordance with the Traffic Guidance Schemes. Posts and bollards
shall be a minimum of 1000 mm. high, capable of being fixed to the road pavement by a suitable road
adhesive or by fastening bolts or spikes. Fixing shall be in accordance with manufacturer’s
recommendations. All posts or bollards will be inspected daily and where displaced or missing made good
immediately. All delineator posts are to be completely removed at the completion of all stages of
construction and prior to the placement of asphalt surfacing. If adhesive is used to affix the posts this shall
be completely removed from the road surface so that a flush surface is obtained.

The spacing between delineation devices should be as detailed in AGTTM Part 3: Static Worksites Table
4.2. These are maximum measurements and can be reduced (e.g on curves at night). If there is a risk that
road users may take a wrong turn or take the wrong path, the spacing may be reduced to a minimum of
1m.

7.4     Site Access for Works Vehicles
When determining methods of entry and exit to the worksite, the following shall be considered:
    • approach routes
    • where possible avoid placing access points on curves
    • visibility at the access point (e.g. where fences or signs obstruct sight distance) shall ensure that
         traffic entering or leaving the worksite can see and be seen by other road users, and that vulnerable
         road users such as children, are visible to traffic entering or leaving the site
    • sight distance to access points in or out of the worksite to pedestrian or cyclist paths to prevent
         conflict
    • a clearly determined site entrance for all approaching vehicles that is clearly communicated and
         delineated.
    • radio communication between traffic management crew and worksite traffic
    • the differing speeds of work vehicles and general traffic
    • deceleration and acceleration zones either side of an access point for work vehicles entering and
         exiting the worksite
    • the need for general traffic to be stopped for work vehicles entering and exiting
    • additional acceleration lane for vehicles exiting the worksite
    • the need for multiple access points for entry and exit
    • additional special access points for heavy or over-dimensional vehicles (e.g. construction, work
         vehicles) that have difficulty entering and leaving a normal access point
    • the assistance of traffic control (e.g. traffic controller or portable device) at entry and exit points.
Access points should be located a minimum distance equal to the speed limit measured from the access
point to any intersection, on or off-ramp, taper or other obstruction that restricts visibility to the access
point. For example, a speed limit of 70 km/h requires the access point to be located a minimum distance of
70 m from the large tree obstructing the visibility of approaching vehicles, to the access point. This
guidance is for access points only and not to be used for sight distance to a sign.
Entry and exit of vehicles through an access point should occur in the direction of general traffic flow with
their vehicle mounted flashing lamps switched on to warn road users. Vehicles may reverse into a closure
where risks are managed, traffic volumes are low enough and there is traffic control in place to ensure the
vehicle itself is not a hazard and safety is provided for road workers and road users.
Vehicles leaving a site at a signal-controlled intersection, through a red signal, shall be deemed to be
entering the public road illegally. As such, an alternative exit point shall be located away from the signal-
controlled intersection at a minimum distance equal to the speed.
At all times, work vehicles are to comply with the road traffic code when conducting themselves to and
from worksites an example is as follows:
   • Access points shall be notified to work personnel and suppliers and vehicles shall:
         •        Decelerate slowly and signal their intention by indicator to leave the traffic stream;
         •        Activate the vehicle’s rotating yellow lamp, once a speed of 20 km/h. has been reached
                  and at least 50m prior to the exit location.
         •        Switch on the vehicle hazard lights once the vehicle is stationary.
         •        Where risks associated with unassisted exit or entry to or from the traffic stream are
                  high, Traffic Controllers are to assist entry and exit movements.
   • Vehicles fitted with rotating amber lamps shall have the vehicle’s rotating lamp activated prior to
     entering the traffic stream and shall undertake the following:
         •        Switch off the vehicle hazard lights;

 Traffic Management Plan 0922-01531 Rev. 6              OFFICIAL                               106 | P a g e
           •    Indicate intention to enter the traffic stream using direction indicators;
           •    Ensure there is a suitable gap from oncoming traffic to allow for a safe entry manoeuvre;
                and,
        •       Turn off the rotating yellow lamp(s) once driving at 40 km/h speed limit.
   • When in close proximity to intersections performance of entry and exit manoeuvres are not to be
     completed. Work personnel shall not cross traffic streams on foot unless necessary.

Both construction and traffic management vehicles are required to only park within the work area
indicated on the Traffic Guidance Scheme as the work area. Vehicles shall not obstruct paths and be
parked an adequate distance from intersections or driveways to ensure clear sight lines remain for all road
users.

7.5     Communicating Traffic Management Plan Requirements
The requirements of the Traffic Management Plan and all associated Traffic Guidance Schemes must be
communicated on-site by either the Delivery Supervisor or Site Supervisor prior to the implementation of
any Temporary Traffic Management Devices.

A site-specific risk assessment must be completed prior to the works commencing considering:
    • The action plans for the residual risks from the Traffic Management Plan.
    • The site conditions.
    • Existing Traffic Management infrastructure such as electronic devices and ITS.
    • The installation procedure.
    • The operation of the TGSs once implemented.
    • The removal procedure.
    • The possibility of the setup being left unattended.
The risk assessment needs to be relevant to the type of traffic E.G:
    • The volume of traffic.
    • The speed of traffic.
    • The duration of work.
    • The type of work.
    • Heavy haulage
    • Wide loads
    • PTA Buses
This risk register and site-specific assessment must form part of the Temporary Traffic Management
Toolbox Talks. All persons involved with Temporary Traffic Management activities must be
briefed/inducted by the Traffic Management Supervisor and have the documented on the site records.
The primary objective of the Toolbox Talks is to explain the following to Temporary Traffic Management
staff:
    • Key aspects of the Traffic Management Plan.
    • Identify any site-specific hazards.
    • Temporary Traffic Management requirements for the worksite.
    • Safe workplace requirements and limits.

8.       EMERGENCY ARRANGEMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES
8.1        Traffic Incident Procedures
All traffic incidents shall be reported to MRWA and incident reports are to be made available to the
Delivery Supervisor or the contractor WHS rep within 48 hours of the incident occurring.

In the event of an incident or accident, whether or not involving traffic or road users, all work shall cease
and traffic shall be stopped as necessary to avoid further deterioration of the situation. First Aid shall be
administered as necessary, and medical assistance shall be called for if required.

Road plant within the work area that may impact on any services requiring access to a crash site will be
cleared from the area quickly as necessary.

8.1.1    Serious Injury or Fatality
In the case of serious injury or fatality occurring within the traffic management site all work shall cease
immediately, machinery and vehicles turned off and the area cleared of personnel as soon as possible.
Additional Traffic Controllers (and other personnel if necessary) shall be deployed immediately to ensure
no traffic or other road users approach the area.

The TM crew leader shall contact RNOC 138 138 (Metropolitan state roads and signals) or Main Roads
Customer Information Centre (CIC) (Regional state roads). An Ambulance and Police shall be called on
telephone number 000 where life threatening injuries are apparent. All road workers and traffic
management personnel shall preserve the scene leaving everything in situ, until direction is given by Police
or WorkSafe.

A contingency site-specific detour route and/or road closure point will be determined in consultation with
Main Roads Incident Managers (RNOC for Metropolitan region), signed and controlled by traffic
management personnel and advised to Police, who will take charge of the site upon arrival. Detour routes
will be determined so as to cater for all types of vehicles required to use them. An example of how to
manage an emergency can be found in AGTTM Part 10, section 5.

8.1.2    Minor Incident or Vehicle Break Down within Site
Broken down vehicles and vehicles involved in minor non-injury crashes shall be temporarily moved to the
verge as soon as possible after details of the crash locations have been gathered and noted. Where
necessary to maintain traffic flow, vehicles shall be temporarily moved into the closed section of the work
area behind the cones, providing there is no risk to vehicles and their occupants or workers. Suitable
recovery systems shall be used to facilitate prompt removal of broken down or crashed vehicles.
Caution should be taken when dealing with EV’s (Electric Vehicles) as thermal runaway an toxic fumes pose
a threat, these issues whould be reported through DFES.
Assistance shall be rendered to ensure the impact of the incident on the network is minimised.

Any traffic crash resulting in non-life threatening injury shall be reported to the WA Police Service on 131
444.

Details of all incidents and accidents shall be reported to the Site Supervisor and Delivery Supervisor using
the incident report form at Appendix “C” (or similar).




 Traffic Management Plan 0922-01531 Rev. 6               OFFICIAL                               108 | P a g e
8.2      Emergency Services
Notification to the Emergency services via DFES of the proposed works nature, location, date and times as
well as contact details for the site supervisor.

On-site traffic controllers will be equipped with mobile communications to advise and/or liaise with
emergency services to ensure a prompt response should the need arise.
8.3      Dangerous Goods
Should any incident arise involving vehicles transporting dangerous goods, all work shall cease
immediately, machinery and vehicles turned off and the area cleared of personnel as soon as possible.
Immediate deployment of traffic controllers (and other personnel if necessary) to ensure no traffic or other
road users approach the area.

Notification must be provided to the Emergency services via DFES of the proposed works nature, location,
date and times as well as contact details for the site supervisor. Completion of a briefing to all site
personnel on evacuation and control procedures is required.

8.4      Damage to Services
In the event of damage to gas services, all work shall cease immediately. Machinery and vehicles turned
off, and the area cleared of personnel as soon as possible. Immediate deployment of traffic controllers
(and other personnel if necessary) to ensure no traffic or other road users approach the area. Notification
to the Police services and relevant supply authority is immediately required. Damage to any other services
shall be treated in a similar manner except machinery may remain operational and access may be
maintained where it is safe to do so. Completion of a briefing to all site personnel on evacuation and
control procedures is required.

8.5      Failure of Services
8.5.1    Failure of Traffic Signals
In the event that damage to traffic signal infrastructure and signals fail to operate or operate incorrectly,
all work shall cease immediately. Deployment of traffic controllers (and other personnel if necessary) to
control traffic movements through the intersection is immediately required. Main Roads Western Australia
- Road Network Operations Centre (RNOC) shall be notified immediately on telephone number 138 111.

8.5.2    Failure of Street Lighting
In the event of damage to the street lighting and fails to operate or operates incorrectly, traffic controllers
(and other personnel if necessary with appropriate temporary lighting) shall be deployed immediately. If
the lighting failure adversely affects road user safety, traffic controllers are to control traffic movements as
required. Immediate notification to Western Power is required.

8.5.3    Failure of Power
In the event that the damage to a power infrastructure poses a risk through live current, immediate
deployment of traffic controllers (and other personnel if necessary) is required to secure the site and
prevent entry to the area affected by live power. Immediate notification is required to Western Power via
telephone number 13 13 51.

is required to be advised to the following relevant authorities (contact details for the site supervisor must
also be provided).

9.        MONITORING AND MEASUREMENT
9.1       Daily Inspections
Prior to works commencing the Site Supervisor must communicate the Traffic Management Plan to all key
stakeholders and affected parties.
On completion of setting out the traffic control measures, the site is to be monitored for a suitable period
of time. If traffic speeds on the approaches to the work site are assessed as being above the temporary
posted speed zone for the work site, the Site Supervisor is to initiate action to modify the approach signage
and tapers in accordance with the requirements of AGTTM/CoP . All such actions are to be recorded in the
Daily Diary. Should road users be observed to continue to travel in excess of the posted speed limit, the
police may be requested to attend the site to enforce the temporary posted speed limit.

The Traffic Management Supervisor at the worksite may conditionally approve changes made to a
complex traffic management plan subject to a risk assessment undertaken using the risk matrix in this
Traffic Management Plan. These changes shall be within the scope and objectives of the Traffic
Management Plan. Any significant changes outside of this will need to be endorsed by the RTM and
authorised by the relevant Road Infrastructure Manager where necessary.

The Traffic Management Contractor shall ensure that all temporary signs, devices and controls are
maintained at all times. To achieve this, procedures in line with the requirements outlined in AGTTM Part 6
will be instituted. The monitoring program shall incorporate inspections:
    • Before the start of work activities on site,
    • During the hours of work,
    • Closing down at the end of the shift period, and
    • After hours.

A daily record of the inspections shall be kept indicating:
   • When traffic controls where erected,
   • When changes to controls occurred and why the changes were undertaken,
   • Any significant incidents or observations associated with the traffic controls and their impacts on
       road users or adjacent properties.

The Traffic Management Contractor shall ensure that personnel are assigned to monitor the traffic control
scheme. Inspections shall at least satisfy the following requirements.

9.1.1     Before works start
     • Confirm Traffic Management Plan and Traffic Guidance Schemes are suitable for the day’s activities;
     • Inspect all signs and devices to ensure they are undamaged, clean and comply with the
       requirements depicted on the Traffic Guidance Schemes;
     • All lamps should be checked and cleaned as necessary;
     • After any adjustments have been made to the signs and devices, conduct a drive through inspection
       to confirm effectiveness.




 Traffic Management Plan 0922-01531 Rev. 6             OFFICIAL                               111 | P a g e
9.1.2   During work hours
   • Designate and ensure that appropriate work personnel drive through the site periodically to inspect
     all signs and devices and ensure they are undamaged and comply with the requirements depicted
     on the Traffic Guidance Schemes;.
   • Attend to minor problems as they occur;
   • Conduct on the spot maintenance/repairs as required;
   • When traffic controllers are on the job, ensure they remain in place at all times. Relieve controllers
     as necessary to ensure attentiveness is retained;
   • During breaks or changes in work activities remove or cover any signs that do not apply (e.g.
     PREPARE TO STOP, Workers symbolic);
   • Re-position signs and devices as required by work processes throughout the day and keep records
     of any changes.

9.1.3   Closing down each day
9.1.3.1 Aftercare is required
    • Conduct a pre-close down inspection, allowing time for any appropriate maintenance works;
    • Remove any unnecessary signage (e.g. Prepare to Stop, Symbolic Workers);
    • Drive through site to ensure no signs and devices are left and the road is left clear.
    • Replace any unnecessary signage with appropriate delineation;
    • Install barriers and lights where required;
    • Drive through site and confirm all signs and devices are operating correctly with no misleading
       visual cues;
    • Record details of inspection and any changes made to layout.
9.1.3.2 Aftercare not required
    • Conduct a pre-close down inspection, allowing time for any appropriate maintenance works;
    • Remove all signage from the site.
    • Drive through site to ensure no signs and devices are left and the road is left clear.

9.1.4   After hours
   • Appoint personnel to conduct after dark checks. Replace any signs / devices not working, missing or
     damaged and record in diary.
   • Appoint personnel to conduct checks on non-work days (e.g. weekends). Replace any signs / devices
     not working, missing or damaged and record in diary.
   • The frequency of inspections needs to align with the amount of traffic management on site,
     weather conditions, vehicle types and volumes, road user behaviour and site specific risks.

9.2     Traffic Management Plan Audits and Inspections
A comprehensive review of this Traffic Management Plan (Refer to front cover) is completed. The Traffic
Management Plan may also be subject to a compliance audit undertaken by MRWA at planning and
implementation stage.

Documentation of the audit findings, recommendations and actions taken is required, along with copies
forwarded to the Project Supervisor and the Road Infrastructure Manager Representative and will form
part of the quality management of traffic management implementation within the contract.




 Traffic Management Plan 0922-01531 Rev. 6            OFFICIAL                               112 | P a g e
9.3     Records
A daily diary recording all inspections including variations to the approved Traffic Management Plan shall
be kept using Standard Forms “Daily Diary”. A video recording of each TM layout and changes must be
made and stored for seven (7) days as per CoP section 5.2.
in the event of an incident onsite this record should be kept for up to 7 years.


The Traffic Supervisor is to record all inspections made on a daily basis and at those times prescribed by
the Traffic Management Implementation Standards. Upon completion of each shift, the Traffic Supervisor
shall provide copies of the daily diary record to the Delivery Supervisor.

The Traffic Supervisor is to record all variations made to the approved Traffic Management Plan on a daily
basis and indicate clearly the nature of and the reason for the variations. Upon completion of each shift,
the Traffic Supervisor shall provide copies of the variation record to the Delivery Supervisor.

9.4     Public Feedback
Customer complaints shall be generated by contacting Customer Information Centre (CIC) on telephone
number 138 138. Delivery Supervisor and/or Delivery Supervisor shall process any issues and document
any findings for future learnings.




 Traffic Management Plan 0922-01531 Rev. 6             OFFICIAL                              113 | P a g e
10.     MANAGEMENT REVIEW AND APPROVALS
10.1    Traffic Management Plan Review and Improvement
This Traffic Management Plan requires reviewing either yearly or at a time where an updated revision of
the MRWA Traffic Management for Works on Roads Code of Practice, AGTTM or Australian Standard
1742.3.

10.2    Variations
Two variation forms are attached with this Generic Traffic Management Plan. A template version of the
variation form has been provided where additional Site-Specific variations are found within the planning
stage. A separate variation to the AGTTM, AS 1742.3 or MRWA CoP form is attached for the two
departures required as part of the Generic Traffic Management Plan.

If required, an approval by the Traffic Management Supervisor must be sought, then an on-site variation
made, and changes recorded in the daily diary. In an emergency, on-site variations shall be made and
recorded in the daily diary, and the Delivery Supervisor notified as soon as practicable thereafter.

Where alterations are required to the design of the Traffic Management, Main Roads Code of Practice
requires the following steps:
For on-site changes of non-RTM endorsed Traffic Management Plan’s (CoP reference 4.2.1)
‘With the exception of repositioning of traffic control devices within the allowable tolerances specified in
AGTTM, where any on-site changes to a Traffic Management Plan are proposed, such changes shall be
endorsed by a person holding current WTM or AWTM accreditation. A copy of all documentation relating
to the endorsement of the changes shall be held on-site by the person managing the works.’

10.3    Approvals, Authorisations and Permits
It is necessary to advise all road users of the forthcoming works, the likely timeframe of the works and the
possible road conditions due to the works. Advice may consist of the following:
     • Main Roads Western Australia (Road Planned Interventions, HVS, etc.);
     • Local Governments Authority;
     • Utility Service Providers (e.g. Western Power, Water Corp, etc.)
     • Public Transport Authority (where impact to bus routes, bus stops and level crossing)
     • Other Rail Infrastructure Manager (e.g. Arc Infrastructure).

Any additional approvals must be provided in the Traffic Management Advice by the Traffic Management
Assessor or Delivery Supervisor.
